comparison: Both evaluate claims C59-C65 about β-galactosidase assay data. OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED and convincing for BoxA-mediated antitermination. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether the mechanism is truly antitermination versus an alternative role for SuhB in crRNA maturation, and requesting additional RNAP occupancy data or crRNA processing efficiency tests.

Both evaluate claims C66-C71 about Cascade ChIP-seq data and PAM identification. Both find the data SUPPORTED and convincing, with peer reviewers noting 'the results are convincing' though requesting clarification of statistical methods for some figures.

Both evaluate claims C72-C76 about position-dependent effects of boxA mutation on Cascade binding. Both find the data SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the clear position-dependent effect and BCM reversal. Peer reviewers find results convincing but request statistical method clarification.

Both evaluate claims C77-C83 about CRISPR-I ChIP-seq data. Both find the data SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the position-dependent effect and BCM reversal, acknowledging speculation about an additional promoter. Peer reviewers accept the findings without challenge to the additional promoter observation.

Both evaluate claims about nusE mutant effects (C85-C92 for OpenEval, C85-C92 for peer). Both find evidence SUPPORTED but with concerns. OpenEval notes the nusE mutant has a large chromosomal deletion that could contribute. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting additional experiments to test for relevant Nus factors or clearer text about SuhB versus Nus roles.

Both evaluate claims C114-C118 about type II-C systems lacking boxA sequences. Both find the observation SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the explanation involving repeat-internal promoters is reasonable though not directly tested. Peer reviewers request clarification of which CRISPR Type(s) harbor boxA and how this relates to Lin et al., 2019.

Both evaluate claims C49-C52 (OpenEval) and C50-C52 (peer) about RNAP occupancy in CRISPR arrays. OpenEval finds data SUPPORTED by ChIP-qPCR. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting clarification about the engineered promoter system, natural transcriptional start sites, and relevance of GC-rich Rut upstream of natural promoter.

Both evaluate claims C93-C99 (OpenEval includes C93-C94) about V. cholerae conjugation efficiency demonstrating functional impact on CRISPR immunity. Both find the data SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the strong functional evidence. Peer reviewers found this demonstration convincing without specific concerns.

Both evaluate claims C53-C56 about SuhB ChIP-qPCR data at boxA. OpenEval finds data SUPPORTED, showing robust SuhB association reduced by boxA mutation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether SuhB occupancy alone demonstrates Nus factor involvement, requesting additional experiments or clearer text about SuhB versus Nus roles.

Both evaluate phylogenetic analysis claims (C100-C107 for OpenEval, C102-C103, C107 for peer). OpenEval finds the identification of boxA in 52 genera SUPPORTED with appropriately conservative analysis. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising significant concerns about computational approach assuming arrays downstream of cas2, requesting unbiased search upstream of first repeat and clarification of which CRISPR Types harbor boxA.

Both evaluate claim C132 about Rho termination providing selective pressure against array length. OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as a reasonable inference from data though not directly tested. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, stating 'the possible role of Rho in limiting adaption seems indirect at best' and noting Nus would have opposing impact, requesting speculation be omitted from Abstract.

Both address phylogenetic analysis with partial overlap on C101. OpenEval evaluates C100-C107 as SUPPORTED. Peer R12 focuses on C101 rated UNCERTAIN, questioning why phylogenetic analysis was performed on NusB when SuhB was detected at boxA, requesting analysis be performed on SuhB instead.
OpenEval finds claims C1-C15 (background on CRISPR-Cas systems) SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval finds claims C16-C25 (background on Rho termination) SUPPORTED by appropriate citations to prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval finds claims C26-C41 (background on antitermination mechanisms) SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval finds claims C57-C58 (context for novelty of CRISPR arrays as Nus factor targets) SUPPORTED by citations to prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval rates claims C108-C112 (boxA in cyanobacteria despite lacking rho) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculative explanations without experimental evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rates claims C119-C126 (alternative mechanisms for arrays lacking boxA) as UNCERTAIN, noting largely speculative proposals with no direct evidence for CRISPR context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval finds claims C128-C131 (future directions and applications) SUPPORTED as reasonable speculations and logical extensions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these forward-looking claims.
